title: Shakshuka
skill: Building a sauce, then poaching eggs in it

notes.text: For more than 8, cook it in two 12-inch skillets side by side.

move.title: Sauce first, then eggs
move.body: Build a spiced tomato sauce in one pan, then cook the eggs gently right in it. One pan, and moves you'll use again and again.

why.title: Blooming spices
why.body: Cumin and paprika keep most of their flavor locked up until they meet hot fat. A minute in the oil wakes them up. Much longer and they scorch and turn bitter, so keep the spoon moving.

why.title: Simmering to thicken
why.body: As the sauce bubbles, water escapes as steam. Less water means a thicker sauce and a stronger flavor. When a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a path for a second, it's ready.

why.title: Gentle eggs
why.body: Egg whites go rubbery if they get blasted with heat. A low simmer with the lid on cooks them all the way through. The thermometer proves it: 160°F.

wrong.sign: The sauce is thin and watery
wrong.fix: Keep simmering a few more minutes before the eggs go in.
Start over with fresh oil. Burnt spices make the whole pan bitter.

wrong.sign: The whites are still clear and runny
wrong.fix: Put the lid back on, wait two more minutes, then check again.

quiz.q: Why do the spices go into the oil before the tomatoes?
choices: Their flavor comes out in fat
quiz.explain: Spice flavor dissolves in fat. That's why so many curries and chilis start the same way.

quiz.q: The sauce looks thin. What do you do?
choices: Let it simmer a few more minutes
Turn the heat to high and walk away
quiz.explain: More simmering lets more water steam off, so the sauce thickens.

steps.text: Dice the onion and peppers into pieces about the size of a pea. Mince the garlic: chop it into tiny bits, smaller than a grain of rice, and keep it in its own little pile.
steps.tip: Hold the food with your other hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front. The flat side of the knife slides along your knuckles, so the blade never gets near your fingertips.

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and peppers. Cook, stirring now and then, until soft.
steps.look: The onion turns see-through and golden at the edges.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, and the chili flakes if you're using them. Cook just until it smells toasty, about a minute.
steps.tip: Spices burn fast. Keep the spoon moving.

steps.text: Pour in the tomatoes, {qty:salt} salt, and a few grinds of pepper. Let it bubble gently until it thickens.
steps.look: A spoon dragged across the pan leaves a path for a second.

steps.text: Turn the heat down to low. Use the back of the spoon to make a little well in the sauce for each egg ({n:egg} in all). Crack each egg into the small bowl, then slide it into a well.
steps.tip: Cracking into a bowl first keeps shell out of the pan.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and wipe the counter where the eggs were.
steps.tip: Raw egg can carry germs. Clean hands before you touch anything else.

steps.text: Cover the pan and cook on low until the whites are set all the way through.
Slide the thermometer sideways into an egg white. It needs to read at least 160°F before anyone eats.
Turn off the heat. Scatter the parsley and feta on top if you're using them, and serve straight from the pan with warm pita.
steps.tip: The handle stays hot for a long time. Leave an oven mitt on it so nobody grabs it bare-handed.

soften.text: Warm the olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, peppers, and jalapeños. Cook, stirring now and then, until soft.
soften.look: The onion turns see-through and golden at the edges.

bloom.text: Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, chili flakes, and cayenne. Cook just until it smells toasty, about a minute.
bloom.tip: Spices burn fast, and hot spices give off a sharp smell when they do. Keep the spoon moving, and keep your face back from the pan.

add.text: Cut the jalapeños in half from top to bottom. Scrape out the seeds and white ribs with the spoon, then dice them small, smaller than the peppers. Add them to the onion and peppers.
add.tip: Wash your hands with soap right after cutting the jalapeño. Its juice stings if it gets in your eyes.

wrong.sign: The sauce is thin and watery
wrong.fix: Keep simmering a few more minutes before the eggs go in.
Start over with fresh oil. Burnt spices make the whole pan bitter.

wrong.sign: The whites are still clear and runny
wrong.fix: Put the lid back on, wait two more minutes, then check again.
Crumble feta over it and eat it with plenty of pita; both cool it down. Next time, scrape out all of the jalapeño ribs and seeds.

add.title: Where the heat is
add.body: Most of a jalapeño's heat is in its white ribs and seeds. Scrape them out and it's warm; leave some in and it's hot. The juice stays on your fingers, so wash your hands right after cutting it, before you touch your eyes or face.

chop.text: Dice the onion and peppers into pieces about the size of a pea. Measure the jarred garlic into its own little pile.
chop.tip: Hold the food with your other hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front. The flat side of the knife slides along your knuckles, so the blade never gets near your fingertips.
